instruction: Add the prefix "work_" to the directory name "todo_list_Jan_1" on the Desktop.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

result.command: [ -d ~/Desktop/work_todo_list_Jan_1 ] && echo 'Directory exists.' || echo 'Directory does not exist.'

metadata.explanation: Task requires adding a prefix to the directory name. Evaluator verifies that work_todo_list_Jan_1 exists. Uses existing exact_match metric.

llm_judge_reasons: Incomplete verification: Evaluator only checks if new directory 'work_todo_list_Jan_1' exists, but does not verify that old directory 'todo_list_Jan_1' no longer exists
The instruction requires RENAMING the directory (adding prefix to the name), not copying it
Current evaluator would pass even if agent copied the directory instead of renaming it, resulting in both directories existing
This is a semantic verification gap - cannot distinguish between rename vs copy operations
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Add check to verify old directory no longer exists: [ -d ~/Desktop/work_todo_list_Jan_1 ] && [ ! -d ~/Desktop/todo_list_Jan_1 ] && echo 'Directory renamed.' || echo 'Directory not renamed.'
Update expected value to match the new verification message
This ensures the evaluator verifies both that the new directory exists AND that the old directory was removed (confirming a rename operation rather than a copy)
